harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, cron access is now restricted to root and opsadmin only via /etc/cron.allow, verified before and after a full node restart (boot_id changed, confirming an actual reboot), with cron functionality and the restriction both surviving.
actions_performed: Inspected existing cron config: no /etc/cron.allow existed, /etc/cron.deny was empty (meant everyone was allowed)
Created opsadmin user via useradd -m
Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin' (644, root:root) — cron.allow takes precedence over cron.deny in cronie
Verified a non-listed test user (crontestdeny) was blocked from crontab -l/-e with 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)'
Verified root and opsadmin could both install/list/remove crontabs
Cleaned up test crontab entries and test user
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, crond active status, cron.allow contents, opsadmin identity
Restarted node1 via backgrounded 'sleep 2 && systemctl reboot' so the exec ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed boot_id changed from 15443601-... to 3b4c4dd3-..., proving an actual reboot occurred
Post-restart verified crond active, /etc/cron.allow persisted (root, opsadmin), opsadmin could schedule/list/remove a cron job
Post-restart re-verified a new unauthorized test user (crontestdeny2) was still blocked from crontab, then cleaned it up

evidence.requirement: Baseline: cron daemon, cron.allow/cron.deny state, and users before any change
evidence.summary: crond active; no cron.allow existed; cron.deny empty (everyone allowed); opsadmin did not exist yet

evidence.requirement: opsadmin account created
evidence.summary: useradd -m opsadmin succeeded, uid 1000 created

evidence.requirement: cron.allow restricts scheduling to root and opsadmin only
evidence.summary: /etc/cron.allow created with exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin', correct ownership/permissions

evidence.requirement: Unauthorized users are blocked from scheduling cron jobs
evidence.summary: Test user crontestdeny denied by crontab -l and crontab install with 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)'

evidence.requirement: root and opsadmin retain ability to schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: root's own crontab and opsadmin's crontab installs/listing succeeded

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of test artifacts
evidence.summary: Test crontab removed and crontestdeny user deleted, /var/spool/cron empty again

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline with boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 15443601-befc-4fc4-aa76-b417968ad3f9, crond active, cron.allow contents, opsadmin present

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot scheduled; ack 'reboot scheduled' returned successfully

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node briefly unreachable (connection timed out) then returned with new boot_id 3b4c4dd3-d1c9-4ae2-988e-34ba4c472475, differing from baseline, and new uptime -s timestamp

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron service, config, and access control
evidence.summary: crond active; /etc/cron.allow persisted with root/opsadmin; opsadmin successfully scheduled and listed a cron job after reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart re-verification that unauthorized users remain blocked
evidence.summary: New test user crontestdeny2 denied crontab access after restart; test user and residual process cleaned up

attempts.summary: On node1, cron access is now restricted to root and opsadmin only via /etc/cron.allow, verified before and after a full node restart (boot_id changed, confirming an actual reboot), with cron functionality and the restriction both surviving.
